body_text: The thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland located at the front of the neck, but its influence on the body is anything but small. The hormones it produces help regulate metabolism, heart rate, digestion, body temperature, energy and aspects of mood and brain function. Because thyroid hormones affect so many systems, researchers have increasingly explored whether thyroid disorders may also be associated with changes in personality and behaviour. Recent research has raised an intriguing question: could an overactive thyroid be linked to traits sometimes described as narcissistic, psychopathic or socially difficult? The answer is more complicated than a simple yes or no. What Does the Thyroid Do? The thyroid produces hormones that help control how quickly the body's systems operate. When the gland produces too little hormone, the condition is known as hypothyroidism. When it produces excessive amounts, it is called hyperthyroidism. Both conditions can produce noticeable physical and psychological symptoms. Hypothyroidism may be associated with tiredness, low mood, difficulty concentrating and changes in energy. Hyperthyroidism, meanwhile, can cause symptoms such as increased heart rate, nervousness, restlessness, difficulty sleeping and heightened emotional sensitivity. Thyroid disorders are relatively common, with research suggesting that approximately one in 20 people may live with some form of thyroid problem. This connection between thyroid hormones and the brain has led scientists to investigate whether abnormal hormone levels could also influence personality-related characteristics. Thyroid Problems and Personality Traits A large international study examined the relationship between hypothyroidism and what researchers call Type D personality traits. Type D personality is generally characterised by negative emotionality and social inhibition. More than half of the people with an underactive thyroid included in that research reported higher levels of these traits. However, this does not mean hypothyroidism creates a particular personality type. Instead, the findings suggest that thyroid function and psychological characteristics may be related in some way. The distinction is important because personality is influenced by many factors, including genetics, environment, life experiences, mental health and social circumstances. The question becomes even more interesting when researchers look beyond traits such as pessimism and social inhibition. Could Hyperthyroidism Be Linked to Darker Personality Traits? A smaller study involving 154 adults investigated people with hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism and no diagnosed thyroid disorder. The researchers examined several personality characteristics, including narcissism, psychopathy and sadism. Interestingly, participants with hyperthyroidism showed higher levels of psychopathic and sadistic traits, as well as a smaller increase in narcissistic traits. People with hypothyroidism, on the other hand, appeared broadly similar to participants in the control group. These findings suggest that any relationship between thyroid function and so-called darker personality traits may be more closely associated with an overactive thyroid than with thyroid disorders generally. However, the study was relatively small, and its findings should not be interpreted as proof that hyperthyroidism causes narcissism or psychopathy. Why Could Thyroid Hormones Affect Behaviour? One possible explanation involves the effect of thyroid hormones on the body's overall level of physiological arousal. Hyperthyroidism can place the body in a state of increased activity. Metabolism speeds up, the heart can beat faster and people may experience restlessness, anxiety, irritability or difficulty regulating their emotions. The brain is also sensitive to changes in thyroid hormone levels. Because thyroid hormones contribute to normal brain function, substantial hormonal changes could potentially affect emotional regulation, attention, energy and behaviour. Researchers have therefore suggested that heightened physiological and neurological arousal might make it more difficult for some people to manage impulses or emotions. This is a possible biological pathway, rather than an established explanation for personality disorders. Correlation Does Not Mean Causation This is perhaps the most important point when interpreting research about thyroid disease and personality. Finding an association between two characteristics does not establish that one causes the other. For example, ice cream sales and shark attacks can both increase during hot weather. That does not mean eating ice cream causes shark attacks. A third factor, warmer weather, helps explain why both events become more common at the same time. The same principle applies to thyroid research. If people with hyperthyroidism report higher levels of certain personality traits, several explanations are possible. Hormonal changes could contribute to behavioural changes, psychological distress could affect how people respond to personality questionnaires, or other factors could influence both thyroid health and psychological characteristics. More research is needed to determine whether thyroid hormone changes directly affect specific personality traits and, if so, how. Does Hyperthyroidism Make Someone a Narcissist? There is currently no good basis for claiming that an overactive thyroid turns someone into a narcissist. Narcissistic personality traits exist on a spectrum, while narcissistic personality disorder is a clinical diagnosis involving a persistent pattern of characteristics that can significantly affect relationships and everyday life. A temporary change in mood, confidence, irritability or impulsivity caused by a medical condition should not automatically be interpreted as a personality disorder. Similarly, having hyperthyroidism does not mean that a person is narcissistic, psychopathic or sadistic. The research is better understood as evidence that physical health and psychological functioning can interact in complex ways. Why This Research Matters The findings are nevertheless valuable because they highlight the connection between the endocrine system and the brain. Thyroid disorders can affect far more than metabolism. They may influence mood, energy, concentration, sleep and emotional wellbeing. Recognising these effects can be important when someone experiences sudden or unexplained changes in how they feel or behave. If a person develops significant symptoms associated with an overactive or underactive thyroid, medical assessment can help identify whether an underlying thyroid disorder is involved. Treating the underlying condition may improve physical and psychological symptoms, although treatment should always be guided by a qualified healthcare professional. The Bottom Line Research into thyroid health and personality is still developing. Studies have found associations between thyroid disorders and certain psychological characteristics, with some recent evidence suggesting that hyperthyroidism may be associated with higher levels of traits such as psychopathy, sadism and, to a lesser degree, narcissism. But association is not causation. There is currently no evidence that abnormal thyroid hormone levels alone can make someone become a narcissist or psychopath. Personality is shaped by a complicated combination of biological, psychological and environmental influences. The bigger lesson is that the brain and body cannot always be considered separately. Hormones can influence how we feel and function, and medical conditions can sometimes affect behaviour in ways that are easy to misunderstand. Sources BBC Science Focus, research report on thyroid conditions and personality traits, published 10 August 2026. PubMed, international research examining thyroid function and Type D personality traits Springer, study examining thyroid disorders and darker personality traits Thyroid UK, information on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism. University of Aberdeen, information on the prevalence of thyroid disorders. Disclaimer This article is intended for general educational and informational purposes only. It does not provide medical advice, diagnosis or treatment recommendations. Research linking thyroid function with personality traits is still developing, and associations reported in individual studies should not be interpreted as proof of cause and effect. Anyone concerned about thyroid symptoms, significant changes in mood or behaviour, or possible thyroid disease should consult a qualified healthcare professional for personalised advice.

title: From the desk of Melissa Feldsher: Open banking should be built on trust — not subsidies for middlemen
body_text: From the desk of Melissa Feldsher: Open banking should be built on trust — not subsidies for middlemen By Melissa Feldsher, Head of Consumer Payments, Trust & Security and Open Banking August 11, 2026 SHARE LINKEDIN FACEBOOK COPYLINK EMAIL PRINT Americans are using more digital financial tools than ever — to budget, save, invest, pay, borrow and manage their financial lives in real time. That is good for consumers, competition, and financial services innovation. But it also depends on something basic: trust . At Chase, we support open banking and consumers’ right to access and share their financial data with the apps and services they choose. For our customers, trust is built through the accountability and everyday investments banks make to protect their most sensitive information. For us, this means securely connecting our 25 million customers to share their data with the more than 20,000 apps they choose to use for budgeting, payments, financial planning, and account verification. Trust is not simply about whether data can be shared. It is about how data is collected, used, protected, and governed after it leaves a bank — and whether consumers have meaningful control and confidence their information is accessed only when necessary and only for authorized purposes. When it comes to trusted data sharing, consumer control and consumer protection must go hand in hand. According to a survey conducted by The Clearing House , more than 80% of financial app users are not aware that apps may use third parties to access consumers’ personal and financial information and 78% didn’t know data aggregators regularly access personal data even when the app is closed or deleted. As the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) prepares its next Section 1033 proposal, policymakers face a clear choice: advance open banking in a way that builds trust and strengthens the data sharing system or adopt a one-sided framework that gives data aggregators unfettered access while requiring regulated financial institutions to shoulder the cost of keeping the system safe. The issue is not access. It is who supports the ecosystem. For years, data aggregators, acting as data middlemen, have built profitable businesses on bank-built infrastructure by accessing secure data at no cost, repackaging that data and then charging downstream fintech apps. They monetize access to consumer financial data while expecting banks to build, maintain, and secure the infrastructure — and provide the data itself — at no cost. That's not a foundation for trust. Secure data-sharing infrastructure does not appear out of thin air. Since launching our secure data sharing channels, we estimate we have spent hundreds of millions on building and hardening our data-sharing environment, ensuring a secure way for aggregators, payment processors and fintechs to access our customers’ data. Banks invest continuously in cybersecurity, engineering, monitoring, fraud prevention, resiliency, and customer support to protect customers and their data. A policy that lets one side of the market charge while requiring another to provide access for free is not pro-consumer or pro-competition. It is a government-protected subsidy for data middlemen. We have negotiated data-sharing agreements with 100% of data aggregators who access data through our secure channels. These commercial access agreements and fees offer one real-world example of what a modest, market-based approach can look like. Data aggregators — not consumers — pay just a quarter of a cent on average each time they pull data from our systems. Aggregators charge their clients multiple times more for the same data. Our purpose is simple: ensure all market participants support the secure infrastructure that makes data sharing possible. “ Open banking and market-based commercial agreements are not competing ideas. They are how a secure, sustainable open banking system flourishes. Melissa Feldsher These agreements, based on good-faith negotiations, yielded favorable results for aggregators too. We’ve increased investment to make data sharing faster, more reliable, and efficient, including enhancements to our secure data access channels and processes. In other words, fees help fund the innovation and infrastructure that benefit customers, fintechs, aggregators, and banks alike. Some critics argue that data access fees for middlemen will limit consumer choice and slow innovation. Our experience demonstrates the exact opposite. Since introducing these agreements last year, the number of apps connected through our secure channels has grown by 80%, to more than 20,000 apps, enabling 25 million customers to continue connecting to the financial tools they choose. Customer adoption continues to grow, and data sharing continues to increase. Open banking and market-based commercial agreements are not competing ideas. They are how a secure, sustainable open banking system flourishes. That should be the goal of open banking policy: consumer choice with consumer protection; innovation with accountability; and access with incentives that encourage secure use and lasting consumer trust. What a strong Section 1033 framework should do A strong Section 1033 framework should be grounded in a few common-sense principles: Protect consumers’ right to access and share their data. Consumers should be able to share their financial data and connect to the tools they choose, with clear consent and meaningful control over what data is shared, with whom, and how often. Require transparency from every participant. Consumers should know who is accessing their data, what data is accessed, how often it is accessed, and for how long. Make revocation simple and real. If a customer closes an account or no longer wants a service, the data connection should end. Hold data recipients accountable. Any company that accesses, stores or uses sensitive financial information should meet strong security, privacy, data-use and liability standards. Support secure, modern access. Open banking should rely on secure connections — not outdated practices that put consumers’ information at risk. Avoid mandates that distort competition. The CFPB should not require one group of private companies to provide infrastructure for free while another monetizes access. Such a mandate would undermine resilience, accountability, and fairness in the system. The bottom line The past year has demonstrated that innovation, consumer choice, and responsible data access can thrive together. Consumers continue to benefit from a growing ecosystem of financial apps and services, while industry participants have successfully implemented more secure data-sharing models — evidence that the market is working as intended. We're excited to continue building on that progress. The beneficiaries of a well-designed open banking system are clear: consumers who can safely use the tools they choose; fintechs that can innovate on secure infrastructure; financial institutions that can continue investing in secure access; and a financial system that earns trust by protecting both money and data. The CFPB should build on this momentum by advancing a durable framework built on clear consent, strong security, real accountability, easy revocation, responsible data use and fair, market-based agreements. That is how open banking is delivering on its promise — by building trust. body_text: Michael Sheen has revealed that testing carried out during the filming of his new BBC documentary found toxic chemicals in his blood, a discovery that left the Welsh actor deeply shocked. The 57-year-old actor is investigating alleged environmental contamination in Wales in the upcoming two-part documentary Buried with Michael Sheen . The programme examines claims surrounding the disposal of industrial chemicals and the potential impact on communities living near contaminated sites. Sheen agreed to have his blood tested during the investigation because he expected the results to provide a useful comparison. Instead, the results brought the issue much closer to home. Michael Sheen discovers PCBs in his blood During the documentary investigation, Sheen learned that his blood contained polychlorinated biphenyls, commonly known as PCBs. PCBs are a group of industrial chemicals that were once widely used because of their resistance to heat and chemical breakdown. Their durability made them useful in electrical equipment and a range of industrial applications. However, that same durability has created a major environmental problem. PCBs can remain in the environment for decades and can accumulate in living organisms. The chemicals are now internationally recognised as highly hazardous substances. The World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies PCBs as carcinogenic to humans. Speaking about his test results, Sheen said he had expected the test to show that he had not been exposed. The discovery therefore came as an unexpected shock. He explained that the results made the issue feel considerably more personal and reinforced the documentary's wider questions about how widespread exposure to persistent chemicals may be. What are forever chemicals? The term "forever chemicals" is often associated with PFAS, a large family of synthetic chemicals that are extremely persistent in the environment. PCBs are chemically different from PFAS, although they are also highly persistent pollutants and are sometimes discussed in the broader context of long-lasting environmental contaminants. The persistence of these substances is a major concern because they can remain in soil, sediment and other parts of the environment for long periods. The documentary focuses on claims that historic industrial waste has contributed to contamination in parts of Wales and north-west England. One location examined by Sheen is Brofiscin Quarry in south Wales. The site has previously been investigated because of concerns about PCB contamination. Investigation into Brofiscin Quarry Sheen became interested in the issue after discovering research by farming consultant and whistleblower Douglas Gowan. According to the claims explored in the programme, large quantities of industrial chemicals were deposited at sites across Wales and north-west England over several decades. The documentary also meets residents who live close to affected areas. Some residents reportedly have elevated levels of PCBs in their blood, while the programme explores concerns about serious health conditions within local communities. It is important to note that the presence of a chemical in someone's blood does not, by itself, establish that a particular contaminated site caused an illness. Establishing cause and effect requires detailed scientific and medical evidence. That distinction is particularly important when discussing environmental pollution and cancer. Sheen describes becoming worried after visiting the site The investigation also appears to have changed the way Sheen viewed everyday exposure to potentially contaminated material. After visiting Brofiscin Quarry during filming, the actor recalled becoming concerned that he could accidentally carry contaminated material away from the site. He described returning to his car and removing his boots before cleaning them because he was worried about bringing potentially harmful substances home. The experience demonstrated how investigating environmental contamination can affect people psychologically as well as physically. For Sheen, the concern was no longer simply an abstract environmental story. His own test results had shown that exposure was already a reality for him. Calls for greater responsibility A central theme of Buried with Michael Sheen is accountability. Sheen has argued that those responsible for historical dumping should be required to take responsibility for the consequences. He has also highlighted the difficult position facing local authorities when contaminated land requires expensive investigation, management or remediation. Local councils may face significant financial challenges if they become responsible for dealing with contaminated sites, particularly when historic pollution involves multiple parties and decades-old industrial activity. The actor believes the issue requires a solution that does not leave local communities or councils carrying the burden alone. Natural Resources Wales has previously investigated concerns relating to PCB leaks at Brofiscin Quarry. According to the BBC, the regulator concluded that the leaks did not represent a sufficient risk to justify further action at that time. The documentary could therefore reignite discussion about how historic contamination is monitored and managed and whether communities living near former industrial sites have received adequate protection. Michael Sheen's environmental activism The documentary is another example of Sheen using his public profile to draw attention to social and environmental issues. The actor, who grew up in south Wales, has previously been involved in projects highlighting economic hardship and inequality in his home community. In 2025, he attracted widespread attention after helping clear approximately £1 million of debt owed by people in his hometown of Port Talbot. That project was explored in the documentary Michael Sheen's Secret Million Pound Giveaway . His involvement in Buried with Michael Sheen continues that pattern of using television to investigate issues affecting communities in Wales. When will Buried with Michael Sheen air? Buried with Michael Sheen is scheduled to premiere on BBC Two, BBC One Wales and BBC iPlayer on Monday 17 August at 9pm . The two-part programme follows Sheen as he investigates the history of chemical contamination, speaks to residents and examines claims about the consequences of industrial waste. The discovery of PCBs in his own blood adds an especially personal dimension to the documentary. Rather than simply reporting on concerns raised by others, Sheen has now found evidence of chemical exposure in his own body. Whether that exposure can be connected to any particular source is a separate scientific question, but the discovery clearly changed his perspective on the investigation. As the programme prepares to air, it is likely to generate renewed discussion about PCB contamination in Wales, the legacy of industrial pollution and who should ultimately pay for cleaning up potentially contaminated land. For Sheen, the documentary is ultimately about more than chemicals. It is about communities, accountability and whether people affected by historic environmental decisions should be left to deal with the consequences themselves. Source: The Independent, Rachel McGrath, 11 August 2026. Disclaimer: This article is a written summary based on the source material provided. Claims about PCB exposure, contamination and potential health effects are reported in the context of the documentary and should not be interpreted as proof that a particular chemical exposure caused an individual's illness. Medical or environmental health concerns should be assessed using advice and evidence from appropriately qualified professionals.

title: ZoomInfo reviews: how to evaluate it honestly for demand gen
summary: ZoomInfo reviews usually mean renew-or-replace. See the pros, limits, and evaluation checklist demand gen leaders use before signing another contract.
body_text: When you search 'ZoomInfo reviews,' you're not usually hunting for a star rating. You're deciding whether to renew, shrink the contract, or replace ZoomInfo with something that fits how demand gen runs today. Review sites list pros and cons from hundreds of users. They rarely say which strengths matter for outbound, which limits show up at renewal, or when a contact database is enough on its own. ZoomInfo built its reputation as a contact database with firmographics, direct dials, verified emails, and enrichment that keeps CRM records from rotting. That work is real. Demand gen also needs to know who from your target accounts hit your pricing page this week and which named buyer clicked your LinkedIn ad. Look at your stack through both lenses before you take a renewal call. TL;DR ZoomInfo excels as a contact database for coverage, phones, and enrichment. Live buyer activation is usually a separate layer. Most reviews praise data volume and underweight static decay plus the gap between a list pull and a live buyer signal. Evaluate fit on refresh cadence, CRM sync quality, and whether you can prove pipeline from identified contacts, not logo-level intent alone. Renew when outbound and enrichment are the bottleneck. Pair or replace when you need named site visitors, ad-click identity, or automated audience sync. Use the checklists below before you let a renewal slide on brand familiarity alone. What ZoomInfo reviews are actually trying to answer Most 'ZoomInfo reviews' traffic sits in a narrow window: contract renewal, budget scrutiny, or a stack audit after a missed pipeline quarter. The buyer already knows ZoomInfo is a real vendor with a large database. The useful question is fit, whether the tool still matches how your team sources contacts, enriches CRM, and proves marketing-influenced revenue. That differs from asking whether ZoomInfo is legitimate, which belongs on a separate trust-and-data-quality page ( is ZoomInfo legit ). It also differs from hunting for a longer list of ZoomInfo alternatives . Reviews are the input. Your evaluation framework is the decision. Read reviews for pattern, not drama. A single angry seat is noise. Repeated comments about stale titles, weak CRM sync, or 'intent' that never names a person are signals about stack fit for demand gen specifically. What ZoomInfo consistently gets right ZoomInfo earns its place in many stacks for reasons that show up again and again in practitioner feedback: Contact coverage and direct dials , enough reach for outbound teams that need phones, not just emails. Firmographic and technographic enrichment , fields that make routing, scoring, and territory design less guessy. CRM hygiene workflows , refresh stale titles and fill missing attributes so HubSpot or Salesforce records don't rot. Search and filter UX familiarity , reps and SDRs already know how to pull a list without a six-week enablement tour. Those strengths map to a clear job: build and maintain a contact database for prospecting and enrichment. If your bottleneck is 'we don't know who to call,' ZoomInfo can still be the right answer. Reviews that praise data volume are usually describing this lane accurately. When you interview power users, ask for artifacts, not adjectives: sample lists that produced meetings, enrichment fields that changed routing, and connect-rate deltas after a data refresh. Strengths that can't be shown in the CRM usually don't survive a budget review. If that is the job you need, don't apologize for renewing. Database excellence is not a weak use case. It only becomes a weak stack story when leadership also expects ZoomInfo to identify live buyers on your site, resolve ad-click people, and sync contact-level audiences without another tool. What honest reviews underweight for demand gen The gap shows up when teams expect ZoomInfo to carry activation and proof, not just data. Three limits matter for demand gen leaders even when star ratings look fine: Static data decays. A great export from last quarter is not a live signal today. People change jobs. Titles change mid-cycle. A renewed seat that only refreshes lists quarterly will feel 'accurate' in demos and soft in QBR reality. Lists aren't live buyers. Pulling ICP contacts is not the same as knowing who visited pricing this morning or clicked your LinkedIn ad yesterday. Outbound still needs timing. Reviews that score 'intent' features often blur account-level surges with contact-level accountability. Proof breaks at the person layer. Demand gen needs named people you can put into ads, CRM, and sales sequences, not a warm logo on a dashboard. If your CFO asks which contacts engaged and entered pipeline, account-score theater won't finish the sentence. Static data vs. live buyer signals Database tools and live-signal tools solve different jobs. One answers 'who fits.' The other answers 'who is in market with us right now.' Most ZoomInfo reviews conflate them, which is why teams renew a great database and still miss pipeline from first-party engagement. Clarify the split before procurement drama starts. If ZoomInfo owns prospecting and enrichment, decide explicitly what owns site identification, ad-click revelation, and contact-level audience sync. Missing that sentence is how 'intent' ends up as a checkbox nobody can operationalize. Write the jobs on a whiteboard with sales and marketing in the room: (1) build outbound lists, (2) enrich CRM, (3) identify named site visitors, (4) resolve ad-click people, (5) sync contact-level audiences. Put ZoomInfo next to the jobs it actually owns today. Empty cells are future spend, or honest acceptance that you will not get those jobs from this renewal. How to evaluate ZoomInfo before renew or replace Skip the star-average shortcut. Run a short internal audit tied to how your team actually generates pipeline: What % of SDR dials last month started from a ZoomInfo list vs another source? How fresh are titles when you sample 50 recent opportunities? Does CRM sync create or update records cleanly, or do reps rebuild in spreadsheets? Can marketing prove pipeline from ZoomInfo-sourced contacts, or only activity volume? Which 'intent' features produce named people you can activate this week? Invite sales and RevOps to the same review. Marketing-only ZoomInfo stories miss the people who live in the UI all day. Sales-only stories miss enrichment quality and CRM debt. Capture the answers in a one-pager attached to the renewal thread. Orals get rewritten by whoever is loudest in the meeting. Written jobs and scores keep the CFO conversation grounded when brand loyalty and switching costs start doing the talking for you. A practical checklist Before you sign renewal paperwork, answer yes or no: Is outbound coverage still the primary bottleneck ZoomInfo solves for us? Are we measuring enrichment and list quality, not vanity seat usage? Do we have a separate system for named site visitors and ad-click identity? If ZoomInfo disappeared tomorrow, would pipeline sourcing break, or just get slower for a month? Are we renewing because the tool fits, or because switching feels harder than defending the invoice? Three 'no' answers usually means shrink, pair, or replace, not a reflex multi-year renewal. How different roles should read the same review SDRs care about dials and connect rates. Demand gen leaders care about whether marketing-influenced pipeline can be proven at the person level. RevOps cares about sync quality and field hygiene. Finance cares about cost per opportunity influenced. The same G2 paragraph can serve all four, or none, depending on what you map it to. When you collect internal feedback, ask for jobs, not vibes: 'show me five contacts ZoomInfo helped create last month' beats 'do you like ZoomInfo?' The second question just resurfaces brand familiarity. When ZoomInfo still fits your stack Renew or keep ZoomInfo when your motion still needs a serious contact database and enrichment layer, and you're honest that live first-party activation is handled elsewhere. Pair it when ZoomInfo owns prospecting data while Vector handles who is in market today through site visits and ad engagement. Replace or shrink when you've already bought contact coverage elsewhere and the remaining seat is mostly habit. For landscape context, see ZoomInfo competitors . For evaluation of replacements, start with alternatives only after you've written the job ZoomInfo currently owns. One more renewal trap: seat sprawl. If half your seats never log in, dig into whether ZoomInfo is a company-wide database layer or a small outbound pod tool wearing an enterprise invoice. Right-sizing seats is often a better first move than a full rip-and-replace, and it funds the contact-level activation layer you may still be missing. Finally, put a review cadence on the calendar. Annual renewals reward silence. A mid-year check (same audit questions, same yes/no list) catches decay while you still have leverage, not the week legal needs a signature. The mature stack story is boring on purpose: ZoomInfo (or a peer database) for coverage and enrichment; a contact-level activation layer for named buyers already engaging. Reviews that pretend one product owns both jobs create renewals that look fine on paper and soft six months later. Vector sits on the live-signal side of that split: named website visitors and ad engagers, filtered to ICP, synced into the channels you already run, while a database like ZoomInfo can keep owning coverage and enrichment if that job still needs a dedicated seat. FAQ Are ZoomInfo reviews trustworthy for renewals? Use them for patterns, not as a verdict. Weight repeated comments about data freshness, CRM sync, and outbound usefulness. Ignore single-seat drama. Pair public reviews with your own opportunity sample and pipeline report. Your data should outweigh a stranger's star rating every time. What do demand gen teams like most about ZoomInfo? Coverage, phones, enrichment, and a familiar list-building workflow. Those strengths map to prospecting and CRM hygiene. Not automatically to live visitor or ad-click identity. Where do ZoomInfo reviews overstate 'intent'? When 'intent' means account-level surges that never name a buyer. Demand gen needs people you can put into ads and sequences. Logo warmth without contact identity is hard to activate and harder to prove. Should I renew ZoomInfo or look at alternatives? Renew when outbound and enrichment are still the bottleneck and quality measures hold up. Look at alternatives when you need named site visitors, ad-click identity, or automated contact-level audiences ZoomInfo isn't delivering in your stack. How should I evaluate ZoomInfo before a renewal call? Run the internal audit and yes/no checklist above with sales and RevOps present. Decide the job you need next year first, then compare ZoomInfo's score on that job, not against last year's brand inertia.

title: B2B E-Commerce Platform Replatforming Guide: APAC Playbook for 2026
summary: Step-by-step B2B e-commerce platform replatforming guide for APAC manufacturers and distributors. Covers platform evaluation, data migration, and phased rollout.
body_text: Quick Answer: B2B e-commerce replatforming in APAC requires mapping integration dependencies, evaluating platforms against market-specific compliance and B2B feature needs, executing clean data migration, and rolling out in phased market waves. Budget 8-28 weeks depending on complexity and number of markets. Imagine this: your sales team across six APAC markets is quoting prices through a single portal, customers in Japan see yen-denominated tiered pricing while your Australian distributors get AUD net-30 terms, and your warehouse in Vietnam pushes real-time stock levels to every channel. That's what a successful replatform looks like. This B2B e-commerce platform replatforming guide for APAC works backwards from that outcome to give you a concrete, step-by-step framework—built from the projects we've delivered for manufacturers and distributors across Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, and Australia. Related reading: MR DIY Adobe Commerce to Shopify Migration APAC: Lessons for Retailers Related reading: AI Workflow Automation Platform Funding 2026: What APAC Ops Teams Must Evaluate Now Related reading: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Agents CDP Integration: What APAC Retail Brands Need Now Related reading: Shopify vs Adobe Commerce Platform Comparison 2026: An APAC Operator's Verdict Replatforming isn't a technology decision. It's a business restructuring event disguised as an IT project. According to Gartner's 2024 Digital Commerce survey, 72% of B2B organizations that replatformed cited "inability to support multi-market expansion" as the primary trigger—not performance issues. That matches what we see on the ground. The companies reaching out to us aren't running slow sites; they're running sites that can't handle the complexity of cross-border B2B in Asia-Pacific. Related reading: Haruna Kojima Shopify Plus Cross-Border Growth: How Her Lip To Hit 400% Let's get into the actual steps. Prerequisites: What You Need Before You Start Before touching a single platform evaluation spreadsheet, you need three things locked down. Skipping prerequisites is the number-one reason APAC replatforming projects blow past timelines. Document Your Current-State Integration Map Pull every integration your existing platform touches: ERP (SAP, Oracle NetSuite, MYOB), payment gateways (Stripe, Adyen, local acquirers like 2C2P in Southeast Asia), logistics providers (SF Express, Ninja Van, Australia Post), and any custom middleware. We use a simple YAML manifest to catalog these: 1 integrations : 2 erp : 3 system : SAP Business One 4 version : 10.0 FP2302 5 sync : bidirectional 6 frequency : every_15_min 7 endpoints : 8 - /orders 9 - /inventory 10 - /pricing 11 payment : 12 - provider : Adyen 13 markets : [ HK , SG , AU ] 14 - provider : 2C2P 15 markets : [ TH , VN , PH ] 16 logistics : 17 - provider : SF Express 18 markets : [ HK , TW , CN ] 19 api_version : v3.2 This document becomes your migration dependency checklist. Every item here needs a confirmed path on the new platform before you sign any contract. Quantify the Business Cost of Staying Replatforming proposals die in boardrooms because they lead with features instead of losses. Calculate what your current platform costs you in missed revenue: abandoned B2B carts due to missing payment terms, manual order re-entry hours, markets you can't enter because the platform doesn't support the local tax regime. A Forrester study from Q3 2024 found that B2B companies on legacy monolithic platforms lose an average of 14% of potential digital revenue to platform limitations. Build that number for your business specifically. Align Stakeholders Across Markets In APAC, you're almost never replatforming for a single country. Get sign-off from country managers on a shared requirements document. The biggest political risk we see is a regional HQ in Singapore making platform decisions that ignore Taiwan's e-invoice (電子發票) compliance requirements or Indonesia's NPWP tax ID validation rules. Step 1: Define Your B2B Commerce Requirements by Market Generic requirements gathering kills B2B replatforming projects. You need market-specific, B2B-specific requirements documented before you evaluate a single platform. Separate B2B Requirements from B2C Assumptions Most platform marketing materials lead with B2C capabilities. B2B e-commerce platforms need a fundamentally different feature set: company account hierarchies, role-based purchasing permissions, contract pricing, quote-to-order workflows, minimum order quantities, and credit term management. According to McKinsey's 2024 B2B Pulse survey, 77% of B2B buyers now expect the ability to negotiate pricing digitally. Your requirements doc must specify whether you need CPQ (configure-price-quote) functionality natively or through integration. Map APAC-Specific Compliance and Localization Needs Every market in Asia-Pacific has regulatory quirks that break platforms built for North America or Europe: Hong Kong : No VAT, but Inland Revenue Department requirements for cross-border digital services post-2025 Singapore : GST at 9% (increased January 2024), with specific rules for B2B reverse-charge mechanisms Taiwan : Government-mandated e-invoice integration through the Turnkey Service or approved ISPs Australia : GST on low-value imported goods, specific ABN validation requirements Indonesia : NPWP tax ID validation, local data residency considerations under GR 71/2019 Vietnam : Foreign contractor tax (FCT) implications for cross-border digital sales Document these as hard requirements, not nice-to-haves. Any platform that can't handle your top-three markets' compliance rules is disqualified immediately. Establish Performance Benchmarks by Region Page load performance in APAC varies dramatically. A CDN edge node in Singapore won't help your customers in Ho Chi Minh City as much as you'd think—latency between Southeast Asian countries is often 50-120ms, per Cloudflare's 2024 APAC network report. Set concrete targets: sub-2-second Time to Interactive for your top markets, and test from actual user locations, not just your office. Ready to Transform Your Ecommerce Operations? Branch8 specializes in ecommerce platform implementation and AI-powered automation solutions. Contact us today to discuss your ecommerce automation strategy. Get Started Step 2: Evaluate Platform Options Through a B2B-APAC Lens The B2B ecommerce platform market is crowded, but when you filter for genuine B2B capability plus APAC readiness, your shortlist narrows fast. The Three Architecture Paths Every B2B ecommerce platform comparison eventually comes down to three architecture choices: Monolithic SaaS (Shopify Plus, BigCommerce B2B Edition) : Fastest to deploy, lowest upfront cost, but limited B2B customization depth. Shopify Plus has made significant B2B strides with its B2B on Shopify features—company profiles, payment terms, volume pricing—launched and expanded through 2024-2025. For distributors doing under US$10M in digital revenue with straightforward pricing models, this is often the right call. Enterprise DXP (Adobe Commerce, SAP Commerce Cloud, Intershop) : Deep B2B functionality out of the box. Adobe Commerce (Magento) remains dominant in APAC enterprise B2B—Gartner's 2024 Magic Quadrant for Digital Commerce still places it as a Leader. The trade-off is total cost of ownership: hosting, licensing, and the specialized developer talent required. In APAC, Adobe Commerce developers command US$80-150/hour depending on location, per Robert Half's 2024 Technology & IT salary guide for Asia. Headless/Composable (commercetools, Medusa, Saleor + frontend framework) : Maximum flexibility, but requires significant engineering investment. We see this work well for manufacturers with complex product configuration needs or companies running multiple B2B and B2C storefronts off shared commerce APIs. The Gartner B2B ecommerce platforms analysis increasingly favors this model for organizations with strong internal engineering teams. Scoring Platforms Against Your Requirements Don't use a generic comparison matrix. Weight your scores based on the requirements from Step 1. Here's the scoring framework we use at Branch8: B2B Feature Completeness (30% weight): Company accounts, tiered pricing, quote management, purchase order support APAC Market Readiness (25% weight): Multi-currency, local payment gateway support, tax compliance, language/CJK support Integration Capability (20% weight): Native connectors to your ERP, open API quality, webhook reliability Total Cost of Ownership over 3 years (15% weight): Licensing, hosting, implementation, ongoing maintenance Talent Availability in APAC (10% weight): Can you hire or contract developers in your operational markets? Consider SHOPLINE for Mid-Market APAC B2B One platform worth evaluating that doesn't appear in Western-centric comparisons is SHOPLINE. Originally focused on social commerce in Greater China and Southeast Asia, SHOPLINE has expanded its B2B capabilities and offers native integrations with regional payment and logistics providers that global platforms often lack. For mid-market distributors primarily serving APAC, it can be significantly more cost-effective than Adobe Commerce while offering better regional localization than Shopify Plus. We deployed a SHOPLINE-based B2B portal for a Hong Kong consumer goods distributor in 2024 and got them live across HK, Taiwan, and Malaysia in 11 weeks—roughly 40% faster than a comparable Adobe Commerce build would have taken. Step 3: Plan Your Data Migration Strategy Data migration is where replatforming projects go to die. B2B data is messier than B2C data because you're dealing with company relationships, not just customer records. Audit and Clean Before You Migrate Your old platform has years of accumulated data debt: duplicate customer accounts, orphaned product variants, pricing rules that reference discontinued SKUs. Run a data quality audit before migration. We typically find that 15-25% of B2B product catalog data needs cleanup—incorrect unit-of-measure mappings, missing minimum order quantities, pricing tiers that reference deleted customer groups. 1 # Example: Quick audit script to identify orphaned pricing rules 2 # Assuming you've exported pricing rules and active customer groups as CSVs 3 4 comm -23 \ 5 <(csvcut -c customer_group_id pricing_rules.csv | sort -u) \ 6 <(csvcut -c id active_customer_groups.csv | sort -u) \ 7 > orphaned_pricing_rules.txt 8 9 echo "Orphaned pricing rules referencing deleted groups:" 10 wc -l orphaned_pricing_rules.txt Build a Migration Runbook with Rollback Procedures Every migration step needs a documented rollback path. This is non-negotiable. Your runbook should specify: Data migration sequence : Customer accounts → Product catalog → Pricing rules → Order history → Content pages Validation checkpoints : After each entity type, run automated counts and spot checks Rollback triggers : Define what constitutes a failed migration (e.g., >2% record mismatch, any payment integration failure) Communication plan : Who gets notified at each stage, in which timezone Handle Multi-Currency Historical Data Carefully APAC B2B platforms often have historical orders in 5-8 currencies. Decide upfront whether you're migrating historical orders at original exchange rates or normalizing to a base currency. Most clients choose to migrate order history as read-only records with original currency values, then start fresh transactional data on the new platform. Stripe's 2024 report on APAC commerce found that 68% of cross-border B2B merchants in the region process transactions in three or more currencies—your migration plan needs to account for this complexity. Ready to Transform Your Ecommerce Operations? Branch8 specializes in ecommerce platform implementation and AI-powered automation solutions. Contact us today to discuss your ecommerce automation strategy. Get Started Step 4: Architect Your Integration Layer The integrations are the hard part. The storefront is the easy part. Most replatforming timelines slip because of integration complexity, not frontend development. Design for Asynchronous Communication Don't build synchronous API calls between your new platform and your ERP for everything. A distributor in Singapore doesn't need real-time inventory for all 50,000 SKUs—they need real-time inventory for their top 500 fast-moving SKUs and near-real-time (15-minute sync) for the rest. Use a message queue architecture: 1 // Example: Node.js webhook handler for inventory sync 2 // Using Bull queue for rate-limited processing 3 4 const Queue = require ( 'bull' ) ; 5 const inventoryQueue = new Queue ( 'inventory-sync' , { 6 redis : { host : 'redis.internal' , port : 6379 } 7 } ) ; 8 9 // Critical SKUs: process immediately 10 app . post ( '/webhooks/inventory-critical' , async ( req , res ) => { 11 const { sku , quantity , warehouse_code } = req . body ; 12 await inventoryQueue . add ( 'sync' , 13 { sku , quantity , warehouse_code , priority : 'critical' } , 14 { priority : 1 , attempts : 3 , backoff : { type : 'exponential' , delay : 2000 } } 15 ) ; 16 res . status ( 200 ) . json ( { queued : true } ) ; 17 } ) ; 18 19 // Standard SKUs: batch every 15 minutes 20 inventoryQueue . process ( 'batch-sync' , async ( job ) => { 21 const updates = await fetchPendingUpdates ( ) ; 22 await pushToCommercePlatform ( updates ) ; 23 } ) ; Account for APAC Payment Gateway Complexity B2B payments in APAC are not Stripe-and-done. You need to support: Bank transfers/TT : Still the dominant B2B payment method across Greater China and Southeast Asia Letter of Credit integration : For larger cross-border orders, particularly with mainland China buyers Local payment rails : FPS in Hong Kong, PayNow in Singapore, PromptPay in Thailand Credit term management : Net-30, Net-60, with automated dunning workflows Your new platform needs to handle purchase orders as a payment method, not just credit cards. According to PYMNTS.com's 2024 B2B Payments study, 73% of B2B transactions in APAC still involve some form of offline payment confirmation. Build your integration layer to accommodate hybrid payment flows. Set Up a Staging Environment That Mirrors Production This sounds obvious, but we've inherited projects where the staging environment had none of the regional payment gateways configured. Your staging environment must include sandbox accounts for every payment provider, test connections to your ERP (even if it's a read-only replica), and CDN configuration that simulates multi-market latency. Step 5: Execute a Phased Rollout Across Markets Never go live in all APAC markets simultaneously. We learned this the hard way. Choose Your Pilot Market Strategically Pick a market that's large enough to validate your platform but contained enough to manage risk. For most APAC B2B companies, Hong Kong or Singapore works well as a pilot—both have relatively straightforward tax structures, strong internet infrastructure, and sophisticated B2B buyers who'll give you honest feedback. Taiwan is a poor pilot market due to e-invoice integration complexity; save it for wave two. Run Parallel Operations During Transition For B2B, you can't just flip a switch. Your customers have existing purchase orders, credit terms, and account relationships on the old platform. Plan for 4-8 weeks of parallel operations where both platforms are live. During our migration of a Hong Kong-based building materials distributor onto Shopify Plus B2B, we ran parallel systems for six weeks. The old platform handled existing open orders while the new platform accepted all new orders. We set a hard cutover date, migrated remaining open orders over a weekend, and decommissioned the legacy system on Monday morning. Total parallel period cost roughly HK$180,000 in additional hosting and support—a fraction of the risk cost of a hard cutover gone wrong. Monitor Post-Launch Metrics Relentlessly Your first 30 days post-launch will surface every integration edge case your testing missed. Track these metrics daily: Order completion rate : Should match or exceed legacy platform within two weeks Average order value : B2B AOV drops post-replatform often indicate missing pricing rules or broken tiered pricing API error rates by integration : Spike analysis tells you which integration needs attention Customer support ticket volume : Categorize by "platform issue" vs. "training gap" Ready to Transform Your Ecommerce Operations? Branch8 specializes in ecommerce platform implementation and AI-powered automation solutions. Contact us today to discuss your ecommerce automation strategy. Get Started Step 6: Optimize for Long-Term B2B E-Commerce Growth in APAC The replatform isn't finished when you go live. The first six months post-launch determine whether you actually capture the ROI you projected. Implement Market-Specific Catalog and Pricing Rules Once stable, start building the differentiated capabilities that justified the replatform. Set up market-specific catalogs (not all products are available in all markets—some are restricted by import regulations, others by distribution agreements). Build automated pricing rules that account for local market conditions: a Deloitte 2024 report on APAC pricing strategies found that B2B companies with market-specific digital pricing outperform uniform-pricing competitors by 23% in gross margin. Build Self-Service Capabilities Your Buyers Actually Want B2B buyers in APAC are increasingly expecting self-service features based on their B2C experiences. According to McKinsey's 2024 B2B Pulse, 65% of B2B companies across industries now offer e-commerce as a sales channel—up from 53% in 2021. Prioritize: real-time order tracking, self-service reordering from order history, downloadable invoices and statements, and the ability to manage sub-accounts within a company hierarchy. Plan Your Next Integration Phase Post-stabilization is when you add the integrations that were deliberately descoped from the initial launch: advanced analytics (connecting your commerce platform to a data warehouse for cross-market reporting), marketing automation for B2B lead nurturing, and PIM (Product Information Management) systems like Akeneo or Salsify for centralized catalog management across markets. Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them After delivering B2B e-commerce platform replatforming projects across APAC for six years, these are the failure patterns we see repeatedly. Mistake 1: Choosing a Platform Based on B2C Reviews B2B ecommerce platforms on Reddit and general comparison sites are reviewed overwhelmingly by B2C merchants. A platform that's excellent for a D2C fashion brand will frustrate a B2B industrial parts distributor. Always evaluate with B2B-specific test scenarios: create a company account with three buyer roles, set up tiered pricing for 50 products, process a purchase order with net-60 terms. If the platform can't handle those basics in a demo, it won't handle them in production. Mistake 2: Underestimating CJK Localization Complexity Chinese (Traditional and Simplified), Japanese, and Korean localization isn't just translation. Product search must handle CJK character segmentation correctly—a search for "不鏽鋼螺絲" (stainless steel screws) in Traditional Chinese needs to work as well as the English equivalent. URL structures, breadcrumbs, and meta fields all need to support multi-byte characters without truncation. We've seen platforms that claim CJK support but break when product names exceed 20 characters in Chinese because the database field was sized for Latin characters. Mistake 3: Ignoring the Tax and Invoicing Compliance Until Late Tax compliance is not a post-launch enhancement. Taiwan's Uniform Invoice system requires real-time reporting to the government. Singapore's InvoiceNow initiative is pushing Peppol-based e-invoicing for B2B. Australia requires BAS (Business Activity Statement) reporting alignment. Build tax and invoicing compliance into your platform evaluation criteria from day one, not as a phase-two add-on. Mistake 4: Building Custom When a Connector Exists Before writing custom integration code, check whether your platform and target system have a maintained connector. Shopify Plus has the Shopify Flow + partner app ecosystem. Adobe Commerce has the Adobe Commerce Marketplace. Commercetools has its integration marketplace. A maintained connector at US$200/month is almost always cheaper than a custom integration at US$15,000 to build and US$3,000/year to maintain. Mistake 5: No Dedicated APAC Technical Support Window If your platform vendor's support is US-timezone only, you'll wait 12+ hours for critical issue resolution. Ensure your contract includes APAC-hours support (UTC+8 to UTC+12 coverage minimum) or budget for a managed services partner in-region who can provide first-response support. title: AB’s Active Tax Aware Municipal ETFs May Be a Smarter Long-Term Income Solution Than Cash
body_text: AB’s Active Tax Aware Municipal ETFs May Be a Smarter Long-Term Income Solution Than Cash Cash has been hard to beat in recent years, but sitting on the sidelines carries its own risks in today’s market environment. Key Takeaways Cash has offered a rare combination of yield and stability the past few years, but as interest rates stabilize or start to fall, investors will be forced to reinvest in lower cash yields.
